article.opening: Mars enters Taurus on {{entryDate}} after moving through {{priorSign}} from {{priorSignEntryDate}} to {{priorSignExitDate}}, and action becomes slower but much harder to stop. A task that resisted a quick fix gets another careful pass. A heavy load moves one trip at a time. Once the goal feels worth the effort, we can keep going long after the first burst of motivation would have faded.
article.tension: That persistence costs us when changing course starts to feel like surrender. We keep using the same approach after it stops helping, because changing it would expose how much effort went nowhere. Refusal can stay quiet. We say yes to a plan, then move so slowly that nothing changes. Frustration builds until a small obstacle gets treated like a challenge that must be beaten.
article.development: Mars last moved through Taurus from {{previousResidencyEntryDate}} to {{previousResidencyExitDate}}. The same stubborn effort can show up again now. A stuck repair gets more force instead of a different tool. A familiar routine continues even when it no longer produces the result. In a disagreement, we repeat the same point with more pressure and call that patience. Energy that could move the goal forward goes into defending the first method. By the time anger is obvious, the delay is no longer coming from a lack of strength. It comes from spending that strength against any change in direction.
article.close: By {{exitDate}}, some goals may be unfinished not because effort was missing, but because too much of it went into proving the first way should have worked.
try_this: We can say no to one plan we have been resisting by dragging our feet.
We can retry one stalled task with a different tool instead of adding more force.
We can finish one small physical job this week, such as tightening a loose handle or moving a box that has been sitting in the way.
